data.name: Stones of Sorrow
data.detailed_description:
STONES OF SORROW is a cave painting PDL (Procedural Death Labyrinth).
The game features historic cave paintings, action focused gameplay and brutal executions.

Enjoy the great cave art from Southern Drakensberg, Rochester to Lascaux brought to life in an action-roguelite. All the characters were painted tens of thousands of years ago by our ancestors.

Features:


  • Every time you die, the end boss gains +1 HP.
  • Leaderboards. Only the best player in the world will be able to obtain a Golden Greatsword with Spikes! It deals 666 points of pure damage!
  • Cannibalism! Eat the corpses of your enemies to restore health. But beware, unless you find a special item, you can choke to death.
  • Deranged NPC-s who speak in black metal quotes.
  • The bloodiest & most violent roguelite there is! Ultra juicy gore!
  • Fast, hard, action based gameplay. Watch your stamina bar or suffer.
  • Slaughter grotesque hordes created by the nightmarish imagination of our ancestors.
  • Items and perks of great mystery and power! Gain the edge and crush your enemies!
  • Use collected gold to buy permanent perks for your next life!
  • Level up at bonfires to inflict greater damage, gain maximum health and do faster evasive rolls.
  • CO-OPTIONAL GAMEPLAY - Work together or slay each other.
  • Procedurally generated underground labyrinths.
  • For up to 4 players on a single screen. Play on the same keyboard or use 4 controllers. The camera automatically zooms out when players are far away from each other and back in if players are close.
  • Savage executions for extra 666 gold!

50+ gameplay altering items like:
  • Eating the trader gives you +20 Strength.
  • Every kill makes you +0.1% faster.
  • An evasive roll kills enemies with less than 66% health.
  • More executions = more damage! 0.8% more damage for every performed execution.
  • Touching enemies will make them bleed to death for -10% healthpoints a second.
  • Every hit adds 1% to damage. Resets when being hit.
  • Eating a corpse makes you poisonous for 15 seconds.

Story:

The cave paintings tell an ancient story about a ruthless leader, who slaughtered all the tribes and burned all the lands. His father was murdered at a young age, so the world needed to feel his pain. His closest blood brother helped him rule in fear. But one day he betrayed him and lured him into a maze of torment.
You are that violent ruler. It is up to you to restore your honour. In order to achieve that you must find one of the STONES OF SORROW and brutally crush the skull of your betrayer.

A game solely developed by Rain Pohlak from the Avant-Garde Brutal Death Metal band NEOANDERTALS. All music in the game written & performed by Rain Pohlak & NEOANDERTALS.

reviews.review:
EDIT:
Ready my review.
Read the dev's response.
Bear witness to a great dev, and to how explaining what's what can change the perception of a thing. I hope to change this to Positive.


Wow. 
This game is broken and/or just shit.
If it was polished - er, not even polished, but actually... built instead of slapped together as it seems to have been - it could be great, maybe even rival Apotheon. 
Instead, the game abides by its own rules, which are separate from the ones you are given/told. 


You will do the actions you input only when your character feels like it. 

You can sometimes double-jump and you can sometimes jump until you hit the roof; it seems you have to have the apex of your initial jump be right beside a wal for multiple jumps to be possible (i.e. literally bounding up the wall), but this, too, is finnicky and thus only a guess on my part. 
It seems there is a legit delay in when you hit the attack button and when the attack is executed; this could be attributed to the weapons being heavy - for some sort of immersion - but due to the overall quality of the game, I'd just as soon assume it's because of... shoddy coding(?)
The pause menu has different options such as "Blood" and "Corpses." Whatever option you select just boots you out of the game. 
There is a "View Map" button, which just zooms out so you can get a better feel FOR the arena. Sometimes this works, sometimes it doesn't, sometimes you have to hit it again if you want to zoom back in, sometimes it does so on its own. 
There is a "Dodge." It does nothing for defense. 
Enemies spawn out of nowhere, frequently right on top of you.

There are bonfires to "Rest"/Level-up at (ya); don't seem to really help much - no option for to actually rest (as in regaining some health). 
The game seems an impossible grind - mainly due to how poor the quality is/how little you can trust the game to do what you intend/did on the controller. Cited as "Partial Controller Support," so I may try with KB+M but...

To level-up doesn't really cost a significant amount, but neither do you get a decent amount of Gold (and zero Health Crates). 
When you die, you have the option to buy perks; the cheapest is 3500 - I accrued 3495 after having collected every bit of Gold in the first two maps and from killing all but the last enemy. Too bad the combat is broken.
You can scroll through every perk except the last two, because why not?

The cave walls are a single painting repeated in a tile format.
The music is a grungy, garbled orgy of grotesque.
I feel like the dev might be Swedish; if so, I can't really fault the music. 

I definitely find fault in the game as a whole. 
There is enough of a violent, chaotic cacophony in the soundtrack; Dear Dev Pohlak, please forgive my harsh words. I want to like this game. There's no way that I can right now, nor would I be able to recommend it. I can't speak on how much effort was put into the game, and I do not wish to disrespect you... but I call for mechanic and all-encompassing tweaks/rebuilding. With such rough music, the gameplay doesn't need to be as; streamline it and Stones of Sorrow could become something great. 

P.S. The low price doesn't excuse the quality.
reviews.developer_response:
Hey, thank you so much for playing & taking the time to write a lengthy critique. I really appreciate it. I would like to explain some of my design decisions. I feel like this game is a lot like the early albums from underground metal bands: experimental, twisted, raw and brutal! 

First of all, every action is critically bound to your stamina and if you exhausted your stamina by jumping, dodge rolling or attacking then no further actions or attacks are possible until you regain some of it. Micro managing your stamina during combat is the key for survival. In the last update I increased stamina regeneration while standing +40% and while running +88%. Performing attacks used to be a lot harder and frankly I loved it that way also. The fear of running out of breath and being overwhelmed is something I really enjoy. But it seems to me that new players are not paying attention to the stamina bar (that is rather small & minimalistic) and so I increased the stamina. Increasing it even more would transform this game into a regular button masher.
You can jump six times while in air if you press the jump button quickly in a row. Takes time and skill to master, but can be very rewarding if you can jump around like in a pinball machine. I myself enjoy the vertical freedom it provides. 
Every jump uses stamina and if you fail to quickly push the jump button after a jump is performed, then you will fall to the ground. Originally, in the alpha demo version, I had not this restriction and you could jump indefinitely above the enemies. You could easily escape mobs that way and a lot of the tension was lost. Restricting the jumps to six times makes it a more sadistic experience.
And to answer your question, then no, you do not have to be near a wall to jump like a fast torpedo.
The weapons are huge and every swing takes time. Monsters can only be hurt if your blade has had enough time to move up and gain some of that slaying power. The hitboxes are not even active before that happens.
I experimented around with quicker attack animations and did not enjoy those as much as I did the current animation time. The combat system is built around my personal preferences in an action game. Slow, deadly hits that take time to perform. Double hits are also possible and they do more damage. But beware, double attacks also take more stamina so randomly mashing the attack button will just deplete your stamina. You can attack or double attack while running or standing. Standing still and attacking creates the most damage. 

The pause screen has all the info for the game and how to control it on one screen. The same screen also lets you choose between different settings, like how much blood and corpses you want on the screen at the same time. Lowering those values will increase frame rates for older machines or slower Windows tablets. You select them with your left stick and change the values by moving the stick to the left or right. No need to select them with the A button as that will quit the game. I also wrote that under the control scheme: Press Enter(A) to quit the game. The values are automatically saved.
You can select them with your mouse and use the "A" or "D" on the keyboard. 
On the pause screen there is also info in how to use the "zoom to map" button. It will use 50% of your stamina and can only be used if you have enough stamina. The zoom effect only lasts for a few seconds so you can have a quick look for any dangers or loot around you. Otherwise players would just spam it and that would take a lot of the tension out from the single player experience. 

Using the dodge mechanic is crucial and a very important part of the game. While dodging the player can not be hurt so it provides a valuable escape option for dodging enemy attacks. It can also be used to roll through hordes. There is also an item that makes dodge rolls deadly for any enemies that have less that 66% health.

Enemies spawn around in random rooms and yes, sometimes they spawn on top of you. You will need to use the zoom function to see where enemies are spawning so you can avoid that. I also thought enemies on top of you created a quick reflex based gaming situation where you have a split second to perform an evasive roll.

Leveling up at the bonfires is also important in becoming stronger and reaching the end boss. More Strength means more damage to enemies. More Endurance means more maximum health. Endurance has to be upgraded a lot to show your new max health thought. The new maxhealth is your Endurance multiplied with 0,06. More Agility means faster dodge rolls.

When you want more gold then please execute as many monsters as possible. Enemies of the same type can be executed together at the same time for a lot of gold. You will need to have them all close to you at the same time though. Chaining executions is not always easy, but can be very rewarding. You need full stamina for executions. 
Use instakills for quickly slaying hordes and passing levels. Again, you will need full stamina for instakills. The later levels get very hard without using any instakills. Co-op is a hardcore challenge because instakills are disabled in the multiplayer mayhem.
Health crates can be bought from the trader. Your health needs to be under 25% in order to do that.

The last perk can not be selected with a controller and that is a new bug that came with the 1.1 update. I am sorry for that, I'll fix it with the next patch. Right now it can be selected with the mouse. Again, sorry for the inconvenience. The last box is not a perk but a statistic that says how much your blood brother is amused by your death and how much permanent health he has gained when you have died.

I worked for a year and a half on this game. I feel the price is very cheap for the content provided. Every enemy type can be executed. You have a lot of different items for every playthrough. Some make you as fast as Sonic. Some make you ultra deadly, you only need to touch those monsters and they bleed to death. Performing executions brings your damage up. Eating the trader gives you Strength. Hurting creatures spawns detonating bombs and many more original gameplay changing items and ideas. There are 9 different weapons and according to the Achievement list then no one has gotten the deadliest weapon yet, the Blood Horn. That can only be bought from Little Turnip, the weapon trader. If you want to talk to him, then he has some hidden black metal quotes in his speech and according to the Achievements list, then no-one has talked to him either. Every level becomes bigger and the enemies get deadlier. Some grotesque monsters only appear in the later levels. Every unlocked perk changes the game. Eating corpses and choking to death is brutal! The first perk, which requires 3500 gold, unlocks the change to receive random health crates. The first perk is already a big game changer and giving it too soon to players would just shorten the suffering of the noobs. And I don't want that.  

I'm not Swedish, I'm an Estonian. That is a small country next to Sweden. And yes, I have bizarre and filthy taste in music. I love underground death and black metal and wanted my band's prehistoric crushing music to be as the ultra brutal soundtrack. Most of the music comes from the Neoandertals album "Neanderthals Were Master Butchers". It told a story about the Neanderthals in a time when the cave paintings were originally created. A time of misery & death. I remember the reviews when it came out, it was hated and misunderstood. We worked for four years on the music and some thought it was all improvised. The music sounds like some primitive Neanderthals are going to war.

I disagree, the music is wild and brutal and so should be the game!

Thank you very much and long live the metal underground!
